patient.name: Robert Miller
patient.initial_briefing: You are the attending physician in the Emergency Department. Robert Miller, a 52-year-old male, has just walked in complaining of chest discomfort that started approximately 30 minutes ago. He is breathing but looks visibly uncomfortable and slightly pale. You must evaluate him, gather history, perform examinations, order appropriate tests, and decide on the correct diagnosis and immediate priority.

qa_pairs.fact: Pressure-like chest pain located in the center of the chest.
qa_pairs.answer: It is right in the center of my chest. It feels like a heavy pressure, almost like someone is sitting or pressing down hard on my chest.

qa_pairs.fact: Pain radiates to the left arm.
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, I feel a dull ache radiating down my left arm and up towards my shoulder. It started doing that about 15 minutes ago.

qa_pairs.fact: Pain was triggered by exertion (walking up stairs).
qa_pairs.answer: It started suddenly while I was walking up the stairs to my office. It was so intense that I had to stop and sit down immediately.

qa_pairs.fact: Pain has been ongoing for approximately 30-45 minutes.
qa_pairs.answer: It's been about 30 to 40 minutes since it started. It hasn't let up or changed much since then.
Yes, I have Type 2 diabetes. I was diagnosed about 5 years ago. I take metformin for it.
Yes, I smoke. I smoke about half a pack (10 cigarettes) a day, and I've been doing that for about 15 years.
Yes, I have high blood pressure. My doctor prescribed me lisinopril, which I take every morning.
Yes, I've broken out in a cold sweat. I feel quite clammy and cold right now.
I do feel quite nauseous, like my stomach is turning. I haven't thrown up, but I feel like I might.

qa_pairs.fact: Father had a myocardial infarction at age 54.
qa_pairs.answer: My father had a heart attack when he was 54 years old. He had to undergo coronary bypass surgery.
I take metformin for my diabetes, lisinopril for my blood pressure, and atorvastatin for high cholesterol.
No, I don't have any drug or food allergies that I know of.
No, I've never felt anything like this before. It's completely new and very frightening.

examinations.name: General Physical Exam
examinations.result: Patient is alert and oriented, but appears moderately distressed, pale, and is sweating heavily (diaphoretic).

examinations.name: Cardiovascular Exam
examinations.result: Tachycardia (HR 102 bpm) noted. Heart sounds are normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops heard. JVP is normal. Peripheral pulses are intact and equal bilaterally.

examinations.name: Respiratory Exam
examinations.result: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes, crackles, or rhonchi. Respiratory rate is 18/min, chest expansion is symmetric.

examinations.name: Abdominal Exam
examinations.result: Abdomen is soft, non-distended, and non-tender. No organomegaly or masses.

examinations.name: Neurological Exam
examinations.result: Grossly intact. Pupil reflexes are normal. No focal motor or sensory deficits noted.

investigations.name: 12-Lead Electrocardiogram (ECG)
investigations.result: ST-segment elevation of 2mm noted in leads II, III, and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in leads I and aVL.
investigations.interpretation: Abnormal ECG showing acute inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).

investigations.name: Cardiac Troponin I
investigations.result: Troponin I is elevated at 1.85 ng/mL (Normal < 0.04 ng/mL).
investigations.interpretation: Significantly elevated troponin levels, confirming acute myocardial injury.

investigations.name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
investigations.result: WBC: 9.8 x10^9/L, Hb: 14.2 g/dL, Platelets: 245 x10^9/L.
investigations.interpretation: CBC is within normal reference limits.

investigations.name: Random Blood Glucose
investigations.interpretation: Mild hyperglycemia, consistent with patient's history of diabetes and acute stress response.

investigations.name: Serum Electrolytes Panel
investigations.result: Sodium: 138 mEq/L, Potassium: 4.1 mEq/L, Chloride: 102 mEq/L, Bicarbonate: 24 mEq/L.

investigations.name: Chest X-ray (CXR)
investigations.result: Lung fields are clear. No evidence of pneumonia, pneumothorax, or pleural effusion. Cardiothoracic ratio is normal. Mediastinum is normal width.
investigations.interpretation: Normal chest X-ray. Rules out tension pneumothorax and wide mediastinum (which could suggest aortic dissection).

investigations.name: CT Angiography of Chest
investigations.result: No evidence of pulmonary embolism. Aorta is of normal caliber with no dissection flap.
investigations.interpretation: Normal CT scan. This test was clinically unnecessary given the ECG findings, resulting in resource inefficiency.
